# Introduction

Most Standardised MedDRA Queries (SMQs) are "simple": a case qualifies as soon
as **one** reported term is part of the narrow (or broad) search. These can be
derived in a single `derive_vars_query()` call, as shown in the
[OCCDS vignette](occds.html).

A handful of SMQs are **algorithmic**. For these, the broad search terms are
split into categories and a case only qualifies if a particular *combination*
of categories is present. The combination is evaluated **across the records of
a case**, so it cannot be resolved by looking at a single record in isolation.

This article shows how to derive such a query in two steps:

1. Use `derive_vars_query()` to flag the full SMQ (narrow/broad) **and** each
   algorithm category as its own query variable. Keeping one variable per
   category in the dataset makes the derivation traceable --- a reviewer can see
   exactly which term contributed which category.
1. Use `derive_vars_joined()` to evaluate the algorithm across all records of a
   subject and derive the final query variable.

## The example algorithm

We use *Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)* as the example. Its algorithm combines the
narrow search with four categories of broad terms:

| Category | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Narrow | Core anaphylactic reaction terms |
| A | Broad terms specific enough to qualify on their own |
| B | Upper airway / respiratory |
| C | Angioedema / urticaria / pruritus / flush |
| D | Cardiovascular / hypotension |

A case qualifies if it includes either

* a **narrow** term **or** a term from **category A**; or
* a term from **category B** **and** a term from **category C**; or
* a term from **category D** **and** (a term from **category B** **or** a term
  from **category C**).

i.e. `A or (B and C) or (D and (B or C))`.

**Note**: *MedDRA is a licensed dictionary, so the terms used below are
illustrative placeholders rather than the actual content of the SMQ. In
practice the queries dataset is built by `create_query_data()` with a
company-specific `get_terms_fun` that reads the real MedDRA database.*

# Set up the Queries Dataset {#queries}

The queries dataset follows the structure described in the
[Queries dataset documentation](queries_dataset.html). Here we start from a
simple term list which assigns each term to its algorithm category, and build
the queries dataset from it. This keeps the mapping between terms and
categories in one place.

```{r}
anaphylaxis_terms <- tribble(
  ~TERMCHAR,                   ~ALGCAT,
  # Narrow (core) terms
  "ANAPHYLACTIC REACTION",     "NARROW",
  "ANAPHYLACTIC SHOCK",        "NARROW",
  "ANAPHYLACTOID REACTION",    "NARROW",
  # Category A - broad terms which qualify on their own
  "CIRCULATORY COLLAPSE",      "A",
  "SHOCK",                     "A",
  # Category B - upper airway / respiratory
  "BRONCHOSPASM",              "B",
  "DYSPNOEA",                  "B",
  "STRIDOR",                   "B",
  "WHEEZING",                  "B",
  # Category C - angioedema / urticaria / pruritus / flush
  "ANGIOEDEMA",                "C",
  "FLUSHING",                  "C",
  "PRURITUS",                  "C",
  "URTICARIA",                 "C",
  # Category D - cardiovascular / hypotension
  "BLOOD PRESSURE DECREASED",  "D",
  "HYPOTENSION",               "D",
  "TACHYCARDIA",               "D"
)
```

The first part of the queries dataset is the SMQ itself, with the narrow terms
flagged via `SCOPE`/`SCOPEN`. This is the standard narrow/broad retrieval which
the algorithm is applied on top of.

```{r}
smq_anaphylaxis <- anaphylaxis_terms %>%
  transmute(
    PREFIX = "SMQ01",
    GRPNAME = "Anaphylactic reaction (SMQ)",
    GRPID = 20000021,
    SCOPE = if_else(ALGCAT == "NARROW", "NARROW", "BROAD"),
    SCOPEN = if_else(ALGCAT == "NARROW", 2L, 1L),
    SRCVAR = "AEDECOD",
    TERMCHAR
  )
```

The second part defines one customized query per algorithm category. These are
the building blocks of the algorithm and are kept in the output dataset.

```{r}
alg_categories <- tribble(
  ~ALGCAT, ~PREFIX, ~GRPNAME,
  "A",     "CQ01",  "Anaphylaxis algorithm category A",
  "B",     "CQ02",  "Anaphylaxis algorithm category B (upper airway/respiratory)",
  "C",     "CQ03",  "Anaphylaxis algorithm category C (angioedema/urticaria/pruritus/flush)",
  "D",     "CQ04",  "Anaphylaxis algorithm category D (cardiovascular/hypotension)"
)

cq_anaphylaxis <- anaphylaxis_terms %>%
  inner_join(alg_categories, by = "ALGCAT") %>%
  transmute(PREFIX, GRPNAME, SRCVAR = "AEDECOD", TERMCHAR)

queries_anaphylaxis <- bind_rows(smq_anaphylaxis, cq_anaphylaxis)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(queries_anaphylaxis)
```

# Example Input Data {#input}

```{r}
adae <- tribble(
  ~USUBJID, ~AESEQ, ~ASTDT,       ~AEDECOD,
  "01",     1,      "2021-03-05", "Anaphylactic reaction",
  "01",     2,      "2021-05-12", "Headache",
  "02",     1,      "2021-02-11", "Circulatory collapse",
  "03",     1,      "2021-04-02", "Dyspnoea",
  "03",     2,      "2021-04-02", "Urticaria",
  "04",     1,      "2021-06-18", "Hypotension",
  "04",     2,      "2021-06-18", "Wheezing",
  "05",     1,      "2021-07-21", "Hypotension",
  "06",     1,      "2021-08-03", "Urticaria",
  "06",     2,      "2021-08-04", "Pruritus",
  "07",     1,      "2021-09-09", "Nausea"
) %>%
  mutate(ASTDT = ymd(ASTDT))
```

# Step 1: Derive One Query Variable per Category {#step1}

A single `derive_vars_query()` call derives all prefixes at once. `SMQ01NAM`,
`SMQ01CD`, `SMQ01SC` and `SMQ01SCN` describe the standard narrow/broad SMQ,
while `CQ01NAM` to `CQ04NAM` identify which algorithm category the reported
term belongs to.

```{r}
adae_query <- adae %>%
  derive_vars_query(dataset_queries = queries_anaphylaxis)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(
  adae_query,
  display_vars = exprs(
    USUBJID, AESEQ, AEDECOD, SMQ01NAM, SMQ01SC, CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM
  )
)
```

Note that none of these variables on their own answers whether the subject
qualifies for the algorithmic query: subject `03` has a category B term on one
record and a category C term on another.

# Step 2: Combine the Categories with `derive_vars_joined()` {#step2}

The algorithm is evaluated at case level, so each record of a subject needs to
"see" the other records of the same subject. This is what `derive_vars_joined()`
does: with `join_type = "all"` each record of the input dataset is joined with
**all** records of the same subject, and the joined variables are made available
with a `.join` suffix.

Because the condition has to hold across the whole case rather than for an
individual pair of records, `filter_join` uses the summary function `any()` ---
inside `filter_join` the joined dataset is grouped by the original observation,
so `any(!is.na(CQ02NAM.join))` reads as *"this subject has at least one category
B term"*.

```{r}
adae_alg <- adae_query %>%
  derive_vars_joined(
    dataset_add = adae_query,
    by_vars = exprs(USUBJID),
    order = exprs(AESEQ),
    mode = "first",
    join_vars = exprs(SMQ01SCN, CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM),
    join_type = "all",
    filter_join =
    # narrow term or category A
      any(!is.na(SMQ01SCN.join) & SMQ01SCN.join == 2) |
        any(!is.na(CQ01NAM.join)) |
        # category B and category C
        (any(!is.na(CQ02NAM.join)) & any(!is.na(CQ03NAM.join))) |
        # category D and (category B or category C)
        (any(!is.na(CQ04NAM.join)) &
          (any(!is.na(CQ02NAM.join)) | any(!is.na(CQ03NAM.join)))),
    new_vars = exprs(SMQ02NAM = "Anaphylactic reaction (algorithmic)")
  )
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(
  adae_alg,
  display_vars = exprs(
    USUBJID, AESEQ, AEDECOD, SMQ01NAM, SMQ01SC, CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM,
    CQ04NAM, SMQ02NAM
  )
)
```

The `order`/`mode` arguments are required here only because more than one
record of the additional dataset satisfies the condition for a given input
record; since `new_vars` is a constant it does not matter which one is
selected.

Walking through the subjects:

* `01` qualifies on the narrow term *Anaphylactic reaction* (rule A). Both
  records of the subject are flagged, including the unrelated *Headache*,
  because the algorithm qualifies the **case**.
* `02` qualifies on the category A term *Circulatory collapse*.
* `03` qualifies on *Dyspnoea* (B) **and** *Urticaria* (C).
* `04` qualifies on *Hypotension* (D) **and** *Wheezing* (B).
* `05` has only a category D term and therefore does **not** qualify, even
  though it is part of the broad SMQ.
* `06` has two category C terms, which is not a qualifying combination.
* `07` is not part of the SMQ at all.

# Variations {#variations}

## Flagging only the contributing records

If the final variable should flag only the records which actually contribute to
the qualifying combination (rather than the whole case), drop the `any()` calls
and express the condition over the record pair instead. The current record's
variables are available unsuffixed and the joined record's with the `.join`
suffix:

```{r}
adae_alg_rec <- adae_query %>%
  derive_var_joined_exist_flag(
    dataset_add = adae_query,
    by_vars = exprs(USUBJID),
    order = exprs(AESEQ),
    new_var = ANAPTFL,
    join_vars = exprs(CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM),
    join_type = "all",
    filter_join =
      (!is.na(SMQ01SCN) & SMQ01SCN == 2) | !is.na(CQ01NAM) |
        (!is.na(CQ02NAM) & !is.na(CQ03NAM.join)) |
        (!is.na(CQ03NAM) & !is.na(CQ02NAM.join)) |
        (!is.na(CQ04NAM) & (!is.na(CQ02NAM.join) | !is.na(CQ03NAM.join))) |
        ((!is.na(CQ02NAM) | !is.na(CQ03NAM)) & !is.na(CQ04NAM.join))
  )
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(
  adae_alg_rec,
  display_vars = exprs(
    USUBJID, AESEQ, AEDECOD, CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM, ANAPTFL
  )
)
```

## Restricting the combination to a time window

The MedDRA algorithm is defined at case level, but a study may want to require
that the contributing events occur close to each other in time. Since the
joined dataset also exposes the dates, this is a matter of adding a condition on
`ASTDT` --- e.g. requiring the contributing terms to start within 7 days of each
other:

```{r}
adae_alg_window <- adae_query %>%
  derive_vars_joined(
    dataset_add = adae_query,
    by_vars = exprs(USUBJID),
    order = exprs(AESEQ),
    mode = "first",
    join_vars = exprs(ASTDT, SMQ01SCN, CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM),
    join_type = "all",
    filter_join =
      any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(SMQ01SCN.join) & SMQ01SCN.join == 2) |
        any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ01NAM.join)) |
        (any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ02NAM.join)) &
          any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ03NAM.join))) |
        (any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ04NAM.join)) &
          (any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ02NAM.join)) |
            any(abs(ASTDT.join - ASTDT) <= 7 & !is.na(CQ03NAM.join)))),
    new_vars = exprs(SMQ02NAM = "Anaphylactic reaction (algorithmic)")
  )
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dataset_vignette(
  adae_alg_window,
  display_vars = exprs(
    USUBJID, AESEQ, ASTDT, AEDECOD, CQ01NAM, CQ02NAM, CQ03NAM, CQ04NAM, SMQ02NAM
  )
)
```

Subject `01` now only has its first record flagged: the *Headache* on
2021-05-12 is more than 7 days away from the anaphylactic reaction, so no
qualifying term is within its window.
